Messages.Author: Ohlmann
Messages.Body:
I was indeed expecting Ravnos to be dead last of the major clan.

On the other hand, seeing Kyaside and Baali behind Ravnos and Assamite does surprise me  Instead, the far maligned Gangrel antitribu are a bit above Ravnos and twice as much present than !Brujah.

Then again, it's a hasty study, since I didn't try to see what thoses decks encompasse ; also !Brujah don't have a deck-defining vampire like Enkidu.

On the same hasty level of analysis, clans with a camarilla and a sabbat version with the same discipline (i.e. not the !gangrel and !ventrue that have significantly different discipline payload) almost alway have the camarila version much more present ; my opinion would tie this to three advantages :
* 2nd Tradition, which mean any clan with Prince can have a pretty though defense. The !Brujah are particulary noteworthy on that (even if the Eurobrujah with  also help)
* Parity shift, which is pretty much unrivaled as far as votes go*
* 11-caps with 4 votes and +2 bleed

Messages.Body:
If you have specifics, updates can be applied.

If one clan meets the requirement and has more vampires than any other clan, then only that clan is counted. (i.e. 6 for clan1, 5 for clan2, only clan1 is credited with the win)

A deck would only count twice when in the following situations:  clan1clan2others 552+ 660+ 770+

Messages.Author: Dr.Mafrune
Messages.Body:
I think non-clan decks should be better scrutinized, because more of them can be asigned to a clan.
For example:

1) Decks with anarch converts, can have 4 of the same clan which if you count the crypt without converts the ratio is over 5 12. Therefore converts should not be included in the clan crypt count to see if they have a ratio of better than 5 12 to be classified as a specific clan.

2) There are many decks based on star vampires, which do not have more than four of them. Many times the deck name is named after them, and most of the strategy of the deck is based around them. For example: Nana Buruku with multiple masters, Lutz deck with vampires with innate political actions & black forest base, Anu decks with multiple archon investigations, many salubri decks with heidelberg & spirit marionette, MPA decks with Huitzilopochtli or Cybele or MPA decks with Aksinya Daclau...

3) Decks which the revolves around clan combo. For example: Every Baron deck should be classified as samedi deck even it has only one Samedi.

4) Camarilla & Sabbat clan crossover decks. There are some decks which show different proportions of both clans and are classified in different ways:
Exammples:

a) 5+ vampires antitribu & camarilla. Classified as both antitribu & clan.
b) 5+ clan or antitribu & 4 or the other. Only classified as one.
c) 4 of both clan ( example 4 Dmnitra,3 Armin 1 Hektor). Classified as non-specific clan.

Because slicing the TWDA in various ways is a fun way to waste time, I decided to look at trying to identifier "Superstar" decks. (This is using the twd as downloaded on 2012/10/26, so it doesn't include any of the EC decks yet).

Superstar definition used:  The vampire must be unique. At least 33% of the crypt (so 4/12, 5/13, but not 4/13) Anarch Convert is ignored (because of decks like www.thelasombra.com/decks/twd.htm#2k9erasmusmontpellier ) More than any other unique vampire in the crypt (thus www.thelasombra.com/decks/twd.htm#2012ctbcpj is considered an Unnamed superstar deck) Advanced and base version are considered the same vampire
"Camille Devereux, The Raven" is over-represented from the period when the Jyhad and VTES versions were considered different vampires. I have not tried to compensate for that.
